channel.title: Los Angeles Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Los Angeles Times (latimes.com)

item.title: Canadian snowbirds are still unhappy with Trump. And Palm Springs is feeling the chill
item.description: The decline came in spite of a marketing campaign aimed at Canadians, with Gov. Gavin Newsom emphasizing that the Golden State is more than 2,000 miles from the White House.

item.title: Hit me: California’s blackjack ban could bust L.A. card clubs
item.description: It’s a bust for blackjack in California cardrooms.

item.title: Former L.A. chief deputy attorney directed fraudulent DWP lawsuit, judge rules
item.description: California State Bar Court Judge Yvette D. Roland recommended a two-year suspension for Jim Clark, a former high-ranking attorney under former City Atty. Mike Feuer.

item.title: Lightning fires, avalanches and floods: Deadly string of storms slams California
item.description: Southern California was set for a brief lull in wet weather Wednesday, but forecasters say a new storm is rolling in. Here's what you can expect.

item.title: UCLA must eject Mick Cronin if he can't respect his players
item.description: Mick Cronin's decision to eject Steven Jamerson II for a hard foul late during a UCLA loss at Michigan State shows he's a bully, Bill Plaschke writes.

item.title: Senators decry surge in deaths at ICE detention facilities, citing poor medical care
item.description: Senate Democrats cited a rise in immigration detention deaths since the start of the Trump administration, questioning oversight, medical care and facility expansion.

item.title: Malibu, 'emotionally and physically scarred,' is suing California, L.A., others over Palisades fire
item.description: Malibu is suing the state, the city of Los Angeles, L.A. County and additional public parties and agencies, seeking damages for financial losses sustained in the Palisades fire.

item.title: CBS's Bari Weiss pulls out of UCLA lecture
item.description: Weiss, the founder of the Free Press and now editor-in-chief at CBS News, had been invited to speak at UCLA on the future of journalism.

item.title: Pressure mounts on Wasserman to resign as head of LA28 Olympics
item.description: The state steers money and resources to help the 2028 Olympics and other major events.

item.title: County prosecutors probing whether Edison should be criminally prosecuted for Eaton fire
item.description: The Los Angeles County district attorney is investigating whether Southern California Edison should be criminally prosecuted for its actions in last year’s devastating Eaton wildfire, which killed 19 people and left thousands of families homeless.
